thread:
maria: heads-up — customer reported persistent 401s + occasional 429s when using the Console. They can reproduce in Chrome and Safari. Asking for exact repro instructions we can send them so we get a HAR + console logs + a curl repro.

josh: ok. Quick checklist to request from them: short bullet list in a single reply so it's easy to paste.

maria: yep, please — make it copy/paste friendly.

josh: Paste this to the customer: 
1) Reproduce once in their browser while keeping DevTools open (Network + Console).
2) In Network panel find the failing request (POST to /v1/chat/completions or /v1/responses). Click it -> Headers -> look for any response header like `x-request-id` or `x-rw-request-id`. Copy that value and include it in your reply.
3) Export a HAR (Chrome/Edge/Brave): Right-click any entry in Network panel -> Save all as HAR with content. In Chrome: DevTools ▸ Network ▸ right click ▸ "Save all as HAR with content".
4) For Safari: Develop ▸ Show Web Inspector ▸ Network ▸ Export as HAR.
5) Collect Console: In Console tab right-click -> Save as... (or copy errors). Include the top 20 lines around the error.
6) Curl repro: From DevTools -> Copy -> Copy as cURL (bash). Before sending, redact the `Authorization` header value and replace with `Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>`. Paste the exact curl snippet.

josh: include this example curl they can use to confirm labels (replace placeholders):

```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```

josh: tell them we need the raw response headers for the failing request (don't just screenshot) — headers often contain the `x-request-id` we need to trace.

maria: Add a short howto for HAR+Console export (copyable):

josh: sure — use this block: 

"""
Chrome/Edge/Brave steps:
1) Open the page and reproduce the error with DevTools open (F12).
2) In DevTools, open Network tab. Check "Preserve log".
3) Perform the failing action.
4) Right-click any entry -> Save all as HAR with content.
5) Open Console tab, right-click inside and "Save as..." or select and copy errors.
6) Attach both the HAR file and the console text file.

Safari steps:
1) Enable Develop menu if needed (Preferences → Advanced → Show Develop menu).
2) Develop → Show Web Inspector → Network.
3) Reproduce the issue.
4) In Network, right-click → Export HAR.
5) Console → Copy errors and include them.

Notes:
- Redact API keys and any PII before uploading. Replace API keys with `REDACTED`.
- If they see `429` include timestamps and any retry headers.
- If they see `401`, include the full response body and headers.
- Send HAR + console + curl + request-id in one reply.
"""

maria: good. Also ask them to include the Console error text (e.g. `401 Unauthorized` or JS stack), and whether they are using the Console token or their user API key.

anna: add upload guidance: we prefer customer uploads to the secure support bucket link (internal link below) or they can attach to the thread. If the file is >50MB ask for the signed upload link.

anna: paste this upload paragraph: 
"Please upload the HAR + console files to our secure support upload: https://internal.redwood/support-upload (one-time signed link). If you can’t, attach files directly to this thread. For large files (>50MB) reply and we'll generate a short-lived signed URL for you."

maria: also request browser + version, OS, and exact Console URL (Console -> bottom left shows edition).

josh: last bit — if they can't produce a HAR, ask for a full curl trace with `--trace-ascii` (for advanced users), or they can use `curl -v` to capture headers. Example: 
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' 2>&1 | tee curl.log
```

maria: great — I'll send this to the customer now. Quick question: what exact header keys do we check for request id?

josh: prioritize: `x-request-id`, `x-rw-request-id`, `request-id`. Also sometimes `x-amzn-requestid` if proxied through aws. If they only have a `request-id` in JSON body include that too.

maria: perfect — sending. :thumbsup:

filebot: upload succeeded — har_2111112230_customer-attachment.har attached by maria at 2111112230

maria: thanks team — will follow up when we get the bundle.

josh: if customer returns a HAR without content, ask them to re-export with "Save all as HAR with content". People often miss that.

maria: noted.

(End of thread)
